newsitem.title: COMOROS: OAU team whisked away by Comoran soldiers.
newsitem.headline: OAU team whisked away by Comoran soldiers.

text.p: Comoran government soldiers intercepted an Organisation of African Unity (OAU) team on the secessionist island of Moheli on Wednesday and drove off with the mediators, witnesses said.

They said the OAU mediators led by Pierre Yere of Ivory Coast were intercepted on arrival at Bandar Salam airport shortly after being welcomed by secessionist leader Said Mohamed Souef, who was elected on Monday "president" of Moheli by supporters.
A group of troops who arrived in a rush at the airport then invited the OAU delegation into a Comoran government car and drove the team to an an unknown destination, witnesses said.
An angry secessionist leader, who declined to be named, said the incident might compromise talks with the OAU mediators.
Crowds of secessionist supporters who went to the airport to give a rousing welcome to the OAU team were upset at their disappearance and set up barricades to block the airport road.

A small unit of government soldiers is stationed on Moheli but had not interfered since Souef was elected president on Monday when the island followed Anjouan island in declaring independence from the Federal Islamic Republic of the Comoros.
Anjouan, the second largest island in the Comoros Indian Ocean archipelago, broke away in early August after weeks of unrest. The Comoro Islands have a population of some 670,000 people.
The delegation arrived on Moheli on Wednesday from Anjouan, where secessionist leaders on Tuesday told the OAU mediators their decision to leave Comoros was irreversible.

Islanders on Anjouan, and the smallest island of Moheli, say they want to return to French rule or become independent because they have received little from the government but poverty and numerous coups since Comoran independence from France in 1975.
The poverty in the three islands of Comoros contrasts with comparative prosperity on the island of Mayotte, which voted against independence in 1975 and remains under French rule.

The secessionists said they rejected the OAU delegation's insistence that they respect the integrity of the republic. Yerre said on Tuesday the Anjouan secessionist leaders accepted talks with authorities based in the Comoran capital of Moroni.
The Anjouan secessionists demanded the withdrawal of troops and proposed talks in Mauritius with the Comoran government.

The Comoros embassy in Paris denied on Tuesday government troops would intervene on Anjouan and Moheli and said authorities in Moroni wanted to negotiate peacefully with the separatists to create a more decentralised administration.

Embassy spokesman Mohamed Wadaane admitted the federal system set up at independence had failed and the economy was in crisis. He said the Comoros must decentralise and allow other islands to elect governors and have more control over finances.
President Mohamed Taki announced a plan for more autonomy this month but separatist leaders said it did not go far enough.
